title: One Fall, Three Mechanics
eyebrow: Goosethropic Physics · Mechanics · computed in Rust via WebAssembly
lede: The same bouncing ball, described three ways — and all three are the same fact. Newton sees a constant force; Lagrange sees the one path whose action cannot be lowered; Hamilton sees a point riding a level set of the energy. Change gravity and watch all three descriptions move together, because there is only one motion. Unit mass throughout.

claims.text: The action excess is exactly ε²K — minimum at the flown path.
H is constant along every flight.
Each bounce multiplies H by exactly e².
The phase point this page draws rides its level set.

force arrow / the flown path's minimum

tryThis: Slide gravity to the Moon (1.62): every clock stretches 2.46×, the force arrow shrinks — and not one apex height moves.
Set ε = 1 and press Play: the dashed path is a legal history the ball refuses to have; its cost never leaves the top of the parabola.
Push e to 0.92 and watch the Hamilton staircase become shallow — near-elastic means near-conservative.
Set e = 0.30: two bounces and done. Where did H go? (The page's answer: sound, heat, deformation — the thud.)
footer: closed forms only, nothing stepped · time slider runs in fractions of the rest time · unit mass
card: The bouncing ball through Newton, Lagrange, and Hamilton — force arrow, action parabola, phase portrait — with gravity as a slider, all three views moving together.
cardClaim: F = ma, δS = 0, and dH/dt = 0 are one motion in three notations; each bounce costs exactly e² of H.
